name: cli-init-refuse-existing
body: `kalide init` refuses (clear message, non-zero exit, nothing written) if any of `slides/`, `assets/`, `templates/` or `kalide.yaml` already exists. Other files (e.g. `.git`, or a legacy `eypres.yaml`, which is not recognised) do not block. There is no `--force` flag. The check is independent of the optional path argument: `kalide init <path>` still refuses when a local `templates/` (or any of the other entries) already exists — passing a path never relaxes or widens it, so init only ever seeds an otherwise-empty directory.
